captions.detailed: This 3D model is a long, rectangular pencil box with two symmetrical halves connected by a continuous, interleaved print-in-place hinge. Each half is a shallow rectangular tray with thin walls. On the front edges opposite the hinge, there is a latch mechanism consisting of a cylindrical catch on one half and a pivoting clasp on the other to secure the box when closed.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric, print-in-place pencil box with a hinged lid. The user should be able to adjust parameters such as the box width, depth, height, wall thickness, hinge outer/inner diameters, and latch width.
captions.factory: The design is split into three main modules: bottom(), top(), and bottomLatch(). The bottom and top trays are created by differencing smaller cubes from larger ones to create hollow boxes. The continuous hinge along the seam is constructed using hull() operations between cylinders and cubes, with a for-loop subtracting interleaved sections (using fingerSize and hingeFingerSlop) to create the alternating hinge fingers. A central cylinder acts as the hinge axle, and a similar smaller-scale cylinder-and-clasp design forms the latch on the front.
